title: Zoom in: one truck reading written at LOCAL_QUORUM
caption: Two local acks make the reading durable; the other region is updated in parallel but nobody waits for it.

messages.label: INSERT reading (LOCAL_QUORUM)
messages.note: Primary key ((vehicle_id, day), ts). The token-aware driver hashes the partition key and picks a replica, so the coordinator is also a replica.

messages.label: commit log + memtable
messages.note: B is one of the three local replicas, so its own write counts as the first ack.

messages.label: mutation
messages.note: Sent at the same time to one node in DC2, which forwards it to its local replicas.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: 2 of 3 local replicas: LOCAL_QUORUM is met.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: The third ack arrives later; it doesn't change the answer.

scenarios.name: Node C down: hints
scenarios.summary: One local replica is down. The write still reaches quorum, and the coordinator keeps a hint so C can catch up.

messages.label: mutation
messages.note: Gossip already marks C as down, so B doesn't wait for it.

messages.label: ack
messages.note: B + A = 2 of 3: quorum without C.

messages.label: store hint for C
messages.note: A hint is the mutation plus its target. When gossip sees C again, B replays it (hinted handoff).

messages.label: replay hint
messages.note: If C was down longer than the hint window, hints stop being kept and only repair brings C up to date.

scenarios.name: Timeout, then retry
scenarios.summary: A timeout doesn't mean the write failed. The truck's own timestamp is the clustering key, so a retry overwrites the same row.

messages.label: write timeout
messages.note: A is in a long GC pause and C is overloaded: only B's own write landed in time. A and C may still apply it later.

messages.label: retry, same key
messages.note: Same partition (4417, day) and same timestamp: an upsert of the same row, never a duplicate reading.

scenarios.name: Late batch from a dead zone
scenarios.summary: A truck that crossed a dead zone uploads an hour of readings at once. They land in the right partitions without any read or reorder.

messages.label: split 360 readings by day
messages.note: The batch spans midnight, so it belongs to two partitions: (4417, yesterday) and (4417, today).

messages.label: UNLOGGED BATCH (4417, yesterday)
messages.note: One batch per partition is a single mutation on one replica set. A batch across many partitions would only add coordinator work.

messages.label: UNLOGGED BATCH (4417, today)
messages.note: latest_position is written USING TIMESTAMP set to the reading's own time. Last write wins then keeps the newest position, so a late upload never moves the truck backwards on the map, with no read and no lightweight transaction.
